newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australia Yield Spreads-Outshine the dollar bloc.
newsitem.headline: Australia Yield Spreads-Outshine the dollar bloc.

text.p: Australian bond yields put in a strong outperformance against other dollar bloc bonds as the market squeezed higher after failing to respond to a perkier than expected retail trade report for February.

February retail trade rose 0.8 percent after the 2.7 percent jump in January and when median forecasts had centre a flat outcome. However, some economists had been looking for an increase of up to 1.5 percent.
The Australian/U.S. 10-year bond yield spread fell to its lowest level since mid-March, but the most notable moves were against the Canadian and New Zealand markets.
Canadian debt resumed the recent weak tone as the Canadian dollar came underpressure again on Thursday ahead of the employment reports for both Canada and the U.S. later today.
The Canadian unit has weakened sharply since the Federal Reserve hiked interest rates last week, a move that the Bank of Canada has not followed.
The New Zealand market also extended Thursday's sell-off, which was seen triggered by U.S. investors re-adjusting their portfolios for the new financial year.
